beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier moving through encode, window, repeated compact thought ticks, and decode.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the dense image state from the compact thought process that reads and updates it. The encoder turns the low-resolution input into a dense carrier. Windowing organizes that carrier for local processing without making it sparse. The DQ-CTM stage repeats across ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into the super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR routes dense features through a compact repeated thought process.
params.note: The recurrence belongs to the thought stage itself.

beats.intent: The carrier starts as a dense encoded feature field, and windowing partitions that field into tokens without dropping them.
beats.narration: The persistent carrier begins with an encoder applied to the low-resolution image. The encoder produces the dense feature field that the later process can keep updating. The low-resolution image is the source signal for that carrier. Window partitioning turns the dense field into tokens while keeping every token in the field.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded first, then partitioned into windows.

terms.label: encoder that builds the dense feature field
window partition that keeps every token

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the comparison; at 1.129 million parameters, it is second largest among the five.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison puts the five reported methods on the same million-parameter scale. CATANet is the smallest reported model at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN and IMDN remain below one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is larger than DQ-CTM-SR at 1.592 million parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is second largest by parameter count, not the cheapest.
params.note: Average over five ×4 lightweight super-resolution benchmarks.
